findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff removes the WHERE clause for followed_id, causing the DELETE to remove all follow rows for the follower instead of just the target user, which triggers a conflict (409) when the row for user 3 is already gone or the statement affects multiple rows.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Because the unfollow DELETE now removes all followed rows for the follower, the subsequent GET /api/me/following returns an empty list instead of the remaining followed users.

suspicions.claim: Unfollow deletes all follow relationships where the current user is the follower, not just the one to the specified user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create users A and B. 2. Log in as A. 3. Follow B (POST /api/me/following/<B_id>). 4. Create user C. 5. Follow C (POST /api/me/following/<C_id>). 6. Unfollow B (DELETE /api/me/following/<B_id>). 7. Check following list (GET /api/me/following). Observe that C is no longer followed.
suspicions.evidence: probe s1: typical_user: GET /api/me/following changed: data, pagination.count, pagination.total

suspicions.claim: Unfollow returns 204 success even when the current user was not following the target user, instead of returning 409.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create users A and B. 2. Log in as A. 3. Do NOT follow B. 4. Send DELETE /api/me/following/<B_id>. 5. Observe response status code is 204 (should be 409).
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 attempted DELETE /api/me/following/2 without following user 2, but both base and head returned 401 (unauthorized) instead of reaching the unfollow logic, so the claim about 204 vs 409 was not exercised.

suspicions.claim: Unfollow returns 204 success when the target user does not exist, instead of returning 404.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Log in as any user. 2. Send DELETE /api/me/following/99999 (non-existent user ID). 3. Observe response status code is 204 (should be 404).
suspicions.evidence: Round2 probe for s3 sent DELETE /api/me/following/99999 and both base and head returned 404, not 204, showing the non-existent user case is handled correctly.

suspicions.claim: The unfollow method ignores the 'user' parameter entirely, making it impossible to unfollow a specific user.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create users A, B, C. 2. Log in as A. 3. Follow B and C. 4. Call DELETE /api/me/following/<B_id>. 5. Verify both B and C are unfollowed by checking GET /api/me/following returns empty.
suspicions.evidence: probe s4: power_user: DELETE /api/me/following/3 status 204 -> 409; probe s4: power_user: GET /api/me/following changed: data, pagination.count, pagination.total
